data.title: Largo surges as debt restructuring defuses September bottleneck
data.description:
Largo (LGO) up 21.5% in Friday's trading after saying it signed a binding term sheet with a syndicate of Brazilian banks including Banco do Brasil and Banco BTG Pactual to restructure US$82.2M of outstanding debt, extending the final maturity to March 2030.

Under the proposed revised terms, principal payments will be subject to a six-month grace period, followed by three years of quarterly principal amortization, while interest will be paid monthly.

Largo (LGO) said the restructuring will provide additional time to execute its operational plans and unlock incremental value from its existing operations at the Maracás Menchen mine.

The company said it is focused on ramping up production of copper concentrate and platinum group metals concentrate, progressing toward first commercial sales, and preparing for the first shipment of high-purity vanadium pentoxide to the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency under the US$60M first order announced in July.

data.title: SA Asks: Is CrowdStrike a sell, hold, or buy ahead of its Q2 report?
data.description:
Is CrowdStrike (CRWD) a sell, hold, or buy ahead of its Q2 earnings report next week?

Seeking Alpha analysts The J Thesis, APAC Research, and Amrita Roy weigh in. 

The J Thesis: Sure enough, CrowdStrike (CRWD) remains one of the leading cybersecurity companies. Although I think the cybersecurity landscape has a bright future ahead, underscoring the risks arising from AI capabilities, I find CRWD too expensive at the current price tag.

The tech leader trades at roughly 173x forward P/E, and I feel like the market has run ahead of the fundamentals here. It would need to grow its bottom line by at least 25% annually over the next four years, and it would still trade at about a 65x earnings multiple versus the FY2029 EPS estimate of $2.04. That’s why I give it a Sell rating. 

But don’t get me wrong. Bullish momentum could still carry the stock much higher. Time will tell, but I, personally, don’t like it when the stock is priced nearly to perfection.

APAC Research: CrowdStrike (CRWD) is priced beyond perfection, in my opinion, meaning even excellent performance may not be enough to sustain the valuation. I looked at CRWD a few weeks ago and came away with a Hold, but as earnings approach, my outlook drifts closer to Sell, to be honest. Growth has been pretty slow; net income margins are negative. I expect these numbers to improve, but not enough to justify the valuation.

Amrita Roy: CrowdStrike (CRWD) is a Hold ahead of its Q2 earnings report next week, in my opinion. The stock has already declined over 11% since the time of my last update on August 17th, when I downgraded it to a Hold. The most recent bout of weakness can be explained by the company's CTO leaving to launch a new cybersecurity venture firm. 

On a more fundamental level, CrowdStrike (CRWD) investors would need to see the company deliver a significant beat in both revenue and earnings, demonstrate continued acceleration in Net New ARR, and sizably raise their forward guidance in their Q2 earnings report.

Last quarter, management used the term “Mythos moment” to mark the inflection point for the industry, but at a tactical level, the margin of error is very thin at current valuation levels, making me continue reiterating my Hold stance before the earnings report.

data.title: Trump opens beef imports for 90 days in bid to tame record prices — update
data.description:
Updated 12:00 ET with a  statement from the National Cattlemen's Beef Association.

President Trump is giving beef eaters a reprieve from high prices by lifting the import quotas on imported ground beef for 90 days.

In a social media post, Trump said the U.S. would allow 300K metric tons of ground beef to be brought into the U.S. without paying import tariffs with a “commitment” that it would be sold at 25% below current market prices. The president did not specify where the beef was being imported from, but according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture ((USDA)) the majority of beef imported into the U.S. comes from Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Mexico.

The tariff holiday will make consumers and foreign beef providers happy but will likely face opposition from domestic ranchers who continue to struggle with a 75-year low in the U.S. cattle herd due to a severe drought in the Great Plains and Western states, increased feed costs, and cattle import restrictions from Mexico due to the New World screwworm.  

With the U.S. cattle herd at multi-generational lows, the White House sought to protect domestic ranchers and curb what it called the “foreign-dominated conglomerates that control America’s meat supply” by imposing a 26.4% tariff on over-quota beef imports (imports within the quota face a much lower tariff of $0.044 per kilogram). At the same time, the USDA took steps to rebuild the domestic herd, including expanding grazing on federal lands and limiting the “Product of the USA” label to beef from cattle born, raised, and slaughtered in the U.S.

Since this did little to address the challenges faced by domestic slaughterhouses and meatpacking/processing plants, the Administration lowered the tariff and allowed significantly more beef to come into the U.S. from Argentina under the “Ensuring Affordable Beef for the American Consumer” executive order.  

Unfortunately, Trump’s executive order failed to stop the meteoric increase in the price of beef. Prices dipped slightly in the wake of the E.O. before resuming their advance, reaching a record of $6.89 for a pound of ground beef last month.

In response to the president's proposal, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association ((NCBA)) CEO Colin Woodall called the decision “disappointing” as the outcome to flood the market with government-subsidized, below-market beef "is not the way to rebuild the American cattle herd."

"Today's announcement and other market interventions throw cold water on the prospect of herd expansion and sacrifices long-term stability for short-term messaging," Woodall added.

data.title: Lawmakers ask FDA to scrutinize Chinese trials amid deaths - report
data.description:
• Two Republican congressmen are asking FDA Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas to place greater scrutiny on clinical trial data from China, including not accepting data if a site hasn't been audited recently, amid several deaths reported in studies conducted in the country.
  • Reps. Ben Cline (Va.) and John Moolenaar (Mich.) say that relying on the data could have risks for patients, according to Endpoints News, which obtained the letter. 
  • "In short, the offshoring of early-stage clinical trials to China risks rewarding a system that has shown it is willing to treat children’s deaths as an acceptable cost of faster, cheaper research," the congressmen wrote.
  • The news outlet recently reported on three deaths in three separate trials conducted in China. 
  • The lawmakers are calling on Diamantas to reject clinical data from China for INDs, NDAs, or BLAs except if a trial site has has been audited within a year before an application was submitted.

data.title: OSI Systems' stock drops 10% after Q4 earnings: What went wrong & outlook
data.description:
OSI Systems (OSIS) stock came under heavy pressure after its fiscal fourth quarter 2026 results, falling nearly 10% to ~$197.79 on Friday as investors focused on weaker-than-expected revenue and near-term execution risks.

The stock has now dropped nearly 15% in a week, along with year-to-date price returns of -20.92%, trailing the broader S&P 500 (SP500)'s 11.63% gain in the same period.

The company reported fourth-quarter revenue of $484.1M, down 4% YoY and well below analysts’ estimate of about $529.7M. The main issue was the security division, where about $50M of planned deliveries were pushed beyond the fiscal year-end because of Middle East conflicts and site-access constraints.

The company stressed that these were delayed, not canceled, but investors appeared more focused on when those sales would actually convert into revenue.

Still, the quarter had several strong points. Non-GAAP EPS rose 17% YoY to $3.78, slightly ahead of the $3.77 estimate. The adjusted operating margin also expanded to 17.7% from 15.7%.

OSI Systems also ended fiscal 2026 with record operating cash flow of $275.9M and a record backlog of about $1.9B.

The company also repurchased $123.6M of stock in the fourth quarter and ended the year with $359.8M in cash, giving it more financial flexibility.

Looking ahead, management expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $1.875B-$1.93B and non-GAAP EPS of $11.13-$11.49. Growth is expected to be strongest in the second half, while much of the newer DHS-related business is expected to contribute from fiscal 2028 onward.

With Wall Street maintaining a strong buy rating but Quant rating the stock as a hold, investors may now want to see delayed deliveries turn into actual revenue before sentiment improves.

data.title: Uber faces Europe’s second-largest GDPR fine over driver suspensions
data.description:
Uber (UBER) is facing an €825 million ($966 million) penalty from the Dutch data-protection regulator over the way it used automated systems to suspend drivers, in a case that could become the second-biggest fine under Europe’s privacy law, according to a decision reviewed by Reuters.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority said Uber (UBER) failed to properly inform drivers when computer-driven decisions had significant consequences for their accounts. The ruling covers incidents from 2020 through 2022 and followed a complaint initially filed in France.

Uber (UBER) said it disagrees with both the findings and the size of the penalty and plans to appeal. The company said its current policies provide for human reviews and allow drivers to challenge suspensions.

The dispute centers on Uber’s use of automated systems to flag suspected fraud, including alleged fare manipulation through unnecessary detours and accepting rides without intending to complete them. Uber (UBER) said such suspensions were generally temporary and that permanent deactivations were not automated.

The regulator’s decision also addressed drivers with low customer ratings, with the agency saying some were permanently deactivated by computer. The company rejected that characterization and said 126 European drivers were deactivated for low ratings in 2021.

If upheld, the penalty would trail only Meta’s (META) €1.2 billion GDPR fine issued in 2023.

data.title: Wall Street gains ground as yields calm and Bitcoin extends its climb
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages were firmly in the green on Friday, as Treasury yields held steady and Bitcoin (BTC-USD) saw sharp swings. 

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.8%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.6%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, eight of the 11 S&P segments pushed up into the green and were led by materials, while utilities were the worst performer. 

Treasury yields advanced. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.23%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was higher by 2 basis points to 4.72%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) ticked up 1 basis point to 5.26%. 

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) is seeing sharp swings Friday as the cryptocurrency extends a volatile rebound from below $64K earlier this week.

“After three weeks of strong performance, the S&P 500 is finally succumbing to the usual August volatility that we tend to see this time of year, driven by rising bond yields and confusion about the Treasury's bond purchase program. Bond yields are on the rise, and don't seem to be responding to the Treasury's purchases, largely because the bond market is massive and is pricing in a stronger economy and higher inflation,” Paul Stanley of Arca stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Robinhood Markets (HOOD) climbed higher by +13%, while shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) fell -6%.

data.title: Eric Trump agreed to limit influence on World Liberty Bank plan - report
data.description:
Three World Liberty Financial investors, including President Donald Trump's son Eric, signed agreements to limit their influence on the bank that was recently granted a charter, according to a media report on Friday.

To get federal approval for the national trust bank charter, the three signed "passivity commitments," pledging not to influence the bank's management, Bloomberg News reported, citing documents related to the charter's preliminary approval.

Zak Folkman, who co-founded the crypto business with Eric Trump, and Emirati businessman Hamad Khalfan Ali Matar Alshamsi also made the pledges, the report said.

"World Liberty is intentionally running towards regulation and permanent supervision, not away from it," David Wachsman, a spokesman for World Liberty Financial, told Bloomberg. "Before full approval and for many years afterward, the World Liberty Trust Company will fully cooperate with the OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency), a federal regulator, and will adhere to all other applicable laws and regulations."

President Donald Trump and his family have substantial financial interests in World Liberty; however, the company said they don't hold officer, director, or employee roles, according to the report. The White House has rejected arguments that the president's financial holdings create a conflict of interest.

Dear readers: We recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: AI, chip stocks largely mixed amid broader Wall Street gains
data.description:
Shares of chip and AI-related companies were largely mixed on Friday, while the broader market was largely among gains.

Wall Street’s major indexes climbed as Treasury yields held steady and Bitcoin saw sharp swings. The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) rose nearly 0.56%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) climbed around 0.58%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) jumped around 0.80%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell about 0.63%.

Shares of AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) were largely flat but in the red. BMO Capital began coverage of 12 semiconductor and quantum computing stocks, with bullish views on 10 of them. These included Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Semtech (SMTC), Analog Devices (ADI), and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS). Separately, Nvidia entered into a strategic partnership with data center power facilitator Cloverleaf Infrastructure, which includes a minority investment from the chip giant.

Broadcom (AVGO) climbed about 1%, while Qualcomm (QCOM) and AMD were also in the green. Meanwhile, Cerebras (CBRS) fell about 4%.

American memory giant Micron — which competes with Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) and SK hynix (SKHY) (HXSCL) to provide HBM chips to Nvidia — fell about 1%. Micron's CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said AI has fundamentally changed the memory business, creating a more durable source of demand for an industry historically prone to boom-and-bust cycles. SK hynix's ADR (SKHY) jumped about 1%, while Sandisk (SNDK), Seagate Technology (STX), and Western Digital (WDC) each dipped nearly 1%.

Other AI and networking-related stocks were largely mixed.  Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) slumped about 4%, Celestica (CLS), Corning (GLW), and Lumentum (LITE) each fell nearly 2%, while Ciena (CIEN) and Coherent (COHR) each dipped about 1%. Meanwhile, Cisco (CSCO) rose about 2% while Arista Networks (ANET) climbed around 1%.

Shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) fell about 7% on Friday after a two-day strong rally. Wedbush said that Marvell's announcement this week that it is working with Google to develop custom AI chips is indicative that custom silicon is "advantageous."  Intel (INTC) declined about 2%, while Arm (ARM), Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC), and GlobalFoundries (GFS) each fell nearly 1%. Texas Instruments (TXN) was also in the red. However, Analog Devices (ADI) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) each rose about 1%.

Chip equipment makers:  Applied Materials (AMAT) fell about 2%, KLA (KLAC) dipped nearly 1%, and Lam Research (LRCX) was also in the red. However, ASML (ASML) rose about 1% on Friday.

data.title: Atlanta Braves' short interest climbs on MLB labor dispute
data.description:
Shares of Atlanta Braves Holdings (BATRK) are lower for a second day as shorts continue to pile on as the prospect for a deal between Major League Baseball and the players' union dims into the December 1 deadline.

As reported by Bloomberg, short interest in the Braves’ class C stock (BATRK) has tripled over the last 12 months to as much as 6.8% of float, its highest level since the stock was peeled off Liberty Media Corp. in 2023. This represents a $170M bet against the stock.

The two sides are at a stalemate over a proposed $245.3M salary cap and floor of $171.2M for each team for the 2027 season. The owners are also proposing a 50-50 revenue split between ball clubs and players (consistent with the NFL, NBA, and NHL) along with pooling local TV revenue and a cap on free-agent contracts at five years.

The Major League Players Association rejects the salary cap as "institutionalized collusion" and claims the revenue stream deal would cost players more than half a billion dollars compared to the current agreement. Instead, the players’ union proposes a higher luxury tax threshold, a competitive integrity tax on low-spending teams, and higher minimum salaries.

There is currently no salary cap or salary floor in major league baseball. And according to the MLB, at the start of the 2026 season, only a third of the clubs fall between the proposed cap and floor. 

Short sellers are betting that a deal won’t be reached by December 1, at which time a players' strike would disrupt spring training and the 2027 MLB season.
